description: Transition from the eschatological climax of Az-Zumar (angels encircling the Throne after final judgment) to Ghāfir opening with the Throne-bearing angels interceding for earthly believers, paired with the tetrad of divine attributes.
Transition from the conclusion of Ghāfir on the futility of post-facto faith when punishment strikes to Fuṣṣilat opening with an expounded Arabic Book offering pre-emptive clarity and warning.

Transition from Fuṣṣilat closing with cosmic signs in the horizons and human soul to Ash-Shūrā establishing the universal continuum of divine inspiration across all prophets under the five-letter pivot (Ḥā-Mīm ʿAyn-Sīn-Qāf).

Transition from Ash-Shūrā concluding with the modes of divine speech and the light guiding to the straight path to Az-Zukhruf swearing by the clear Book rooted in the celestial Mother of the Book, deconstructing gilded worldly ornaments.

Transition from the Prophet's cry in Az-Zukhruf ('they do not believe') and the divine response ('for they will know') to Ad-Dukhān unveiling the blessed night of revelation and the terrifying arrival of visible suffocating smoke.

Transition from Ad-Dukhān closing on watchful waiting ('watch, for they are watching') to Al-Jāthiyah marshaling the signs of the heavens and earth and depicting every nation fallen on its knees before the open ledger.

Transition from Al-Jāthiyah concluding with supreme praise and majesty in the cosmos belonging to the Exalted in Might, the Wise, to Al-Aḥqāf opening with the purposeful creation of heavens and earth for a specified term.

Transition from the Makkan conclusion of Al-Aḥqāf commanding patience like the messengers of firm resolve to Sūrat Muḥammad naming the Prophet and initiating the active divine defense and nullification of enemy plots.

The macro-architectural unity of the seven Ḥawāmīm ('Dībāj al-Qur'ān'): all opening with Ḥā-Mīm and the descent of the Book, paired thematically across an intentional concentric structure anchored by Ash-Shūrā at the center.
